# Entry prices with usage packs: a proposal, 18 October 2026

<!-- Generated by `node scripts/pricing-usage-proposal.mjs` from tests/pricing-usage-proposal-table.ts. Do not edit by hand: tests/pricing-usage-proposal.test.ts fails when this file is stale. -->

**A proposal for the owner, not a change.** No price, limit or gate in code changes with it; `PLANS_ON_SALE` stays false behind the tax gate (most-tax reading), the EU art. 9a gate and the commercial review. Every figure below is computed by the repository's own margin code (lib/receiving-costs.ts `unitUnder`, tests/limits-proposal-table.ts `usageCents`, tests/margin-alignment-table.ts `floorPriceCents`, the unit costs of tests/plan-cost-registry.ts); none is typed.

## What it changes, in one paragraph

Today (PR #553) each plan is priced so that every allowance used in full keeps 60%: Store $69, Studio $449, Scale $999 a month, two to four and a half times the competitor plan a buyer sets it beside. The model proposed here, after HighLevel's (a base price, usage charged on top): each plan at an entry price, a smaller included amount of the eight resources that cost money per use (visits, orders, list emails, AI, storage, video hours, access emails, store emails), and every unit above it sold in prepaid packs, each of which keeps 60% on its own. Every limit that costs nothing per use (products, lessons, forms, team, pipelines, 0% of a sale) is kept. **The included amounts are cut, which the owner's rule of 18 October 2026 ("não remover limites visíveis") does not allow without his decision**: the limit is not removed (a pack raises it in the same window), but the figure printed as included is lower than #553's.

## The structure that decides every figure

Under the one receiving model (the dearer of Stripe 6.6% + 30¢ and Paddle 5% + 50¢ on the price plus the buyer's tax on top at 27%, remittance, refund and dispute reserves, at least 27.5% on profit), the 60% floor leaves about 17.24% of revenue for every cost, and receiving one payment takes about 12% of it plus about 60¢ fixed. So:

- **A unit of use must be sold at about twenty times what it costs.** A $29 payment leaves $0.85 for all of its use ($4.15 goes to receiving it). This holds for a plan and for a pack alike, so a pack can never be priced near cost the way HighLevel rebills email.
- **Every plan carries a cost before anything is included**: the studio, the API, webhooks, imports, workflows, team scheduling, the data room and what a store leaves after it closes, all at their enforced ceilings (none of them printed). This proposal keeps all of them, so they set the lowest price a plan can have:

| Plan | Lowest price with nothing per-use included, monthly | The same, yearly | Today's price |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Store | $31.45 | $195.70 | $69 / $690 |
| Studio | $84.25 | $805.75 | $449 / $4,490 |
| Scale | $173.95 | $1,855.90 | $999 / $9,990 |

Store cannot be sold at Stan Creator's $29 without cutting those unprinted ceilings too, which this proposal does not do.

## Every price point looked at

For each monthly price (the year at ten monthly payments), the largest share of every #553 per-use figure (video hours apart: they are kept in full at every price, being the cheapest per-use line, about a cent and a half an hour watched) the plan can include and keep 60% at full use on both intervals, with the room the spend floor test keeps (25¢ a month, $1 a year). Figures are rounded down as a page prints them. "Net a customer" is the monthly payment's net at full included use; "to equal one #553 customer" is how many customers at this price give the net of one at today's price, each at full use: it is the demand the lower price must bring to break even, and **nobody knows whether it would**, because no sale has ever been open.

**The rule for the recommended point**: the lowest price on the list at which every per-use figure is at least 10% of #553's (before rounding down) on both intervals. A lower price wins the comparison beside the competitor's card; below 10% the plan includes too little to read as a plan; everything above the included amount is sold in packs at 60% or more, so a heavy user pays for what they use. This is a rule, not a measurement: the price that maximizes profit depends on how many creators buy at each price, which is unknown until sales open. The table above gives the owner the figure to judge it by (customers needed to equal one #553 customer).

At the competitor's own price instead (Store $35, the lowest that keeps 60% at all, Stan being $29; Studio $99, Stan Creator Pro's; Scale $249, Kajabi Growth's), each plan would include Store 5.5%, Studio 1.8%, Scale 5.6% of #553's per-use figures: nearly everything would be bought in packs, which is HighLevel's own shape (its plans include no email at all).

## The packs

Each pack adds its amount to one billing window of the store's plan, is charged on its own payment before it counts (prepaid: nothing is used before it is paid), and is priced at the lowest whole dollar at which the pack, used in full, keeps 60% on its own with the add-on's 25¢ of room. Its cost is the registry's own unit cost, named in the last column. The same packs serve every plan (a pack's cost does not depend on the plan).

| Pack | Price | Per unit | Cost used in full | Net, sizing reading | Net, most-tax reading | The least a unit can cost at any pack size | Billed on the next invoice instead | Cost basis |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 5,000 visits | **$44** | $8.80 per 1,000 visits | $1.36 | 60.40% | 12.12% | $5.36 per 1,000 visits | $33 | visitCost() (tests/traffic-cost.ts, the heavy visitor) and the REQUESTS_PER_VISIT public requests each visit opens (line public-requests) |
| 250 orders, with their access and store emails | **$35** | $0.14 per order | $0.89 | 60.51% | 12.15% | $0.07 per order | $24 | ORDER_COST, and 0.89 access and 0.67 store emails an order (the most any plan carries per order), at UNIT_COST |
| 2,500 list emails | **$62** | $24.80 per 1,000 emails | $2.25 | 60.30% | 12.08% | $17.76 per 1,000 emails | $50 | PER_EMAIL (line list-email) |
| 20 AI writing jobs and 100 answers | **$50** | $2.50 per writing job with 5 answers | $1.60 | 60.44% | 12.16% | $1.57 per writing job with 5 answers | $37 | WRITING_JOB_MICRO_USD and ANSWER_MICRO_USD (lib/spend-cost-table.ts), the units of the AI ceiling (line ai) |
| 25 GB of storage | **$43** | $1.72 per GB | $1.29 | 60.44% | 12.14% | $1.02 per GB | $32 | STORAGE_PER_GB for the window and the 37 days kept after a plan ends (line retained-files) |
| 20 video hours watched | **$24** | $1.20 per hour | $0.29 | 60.87% | 12.28% | $0.29 per hour | $11 | hourCost() (line video) |

**Beside the competitors:** 2,500 list emails cost $62 here, $24.80 a thousand, against HighLevel's $0.675 a thousand (its pricing guide) — about 37 times as much. That is the twenty-times rule above, plus a pack's own fixed fee; a creator who sends a lot of email will compare it with ClickFunnels Launch (50,000 a month in $97) and Kajabi (marketing emails unlimited) and not buy it. A visit pack works out at $8.80 a thousand visits, where ClickFunnels advertises visitors as unlimited. A larger pack spreads the fixed fees thinner, but no size can go below the column "the least a unit can cost": that is the twenty-times rule alone.

"Billed on the next invoice instead" is the price of the same amount as a line on the renewal invoice, which pays only the fee's percentages: lower, but used before it is paid, so it is a non-payment exposure that docs/funded-exposure-review.md would have to bound and fund first. The proposal is the prepaid pack.

## How it would be enforced, and what is not built

- **The ceilings exist.** Each of the eight figures is already counted and refused past the plan's figure, automatically, before the cost is incurred: visits (lib/traffic.ts, public pages rest), orders (lib/order-admission.ts), list emails and store and access emails (lib/email.ts), AI (lib/ai-spend.ts, the automatic ceiling), storage (lib/storage-quota.ts) and video (lib/video-admission-rules.ts). A pack would add its amount to that window's figure; nothing else would change in how a limit stops.
- **Not built:** buying a pack (a Stripe charge on its own payment), crediting it to the window, the pages that sell it, and its terms. The AI ceiling's company total (`companyMicroUsd`) would have to count packs. A pack's refund would need Hazelsong's rule (refunded only while none of it was used), and the 14-day money-back refund is a funded exposure already bounded by docs/funded-exposure-review.md, which would have to be recomputed at the lower prices.
- **The minimum paying base rises.** Fixed costs are covered by the net each customer keeps above 60%; a customer at a lower price keeps fewer dollars above it, so more customers are needed before the company as a whole keeps 60% (AGENTS.md, "Garantir a partir da base mínima").
- **Nothing opens.** Under the most-tax reading, the gate, no plan and no pack keeps 60% (rows above), exactly as today.

## What is not known

- **Demand.** How many creators would buy at each price, how many would buy packs, and how much of each allowance they would use: none of it is known, because no sale has been open. Every net above is at full use, the owner's rule; real use will be lower, and margins higher.
- **Whether a creator reads a smaller included amount plus packs as more value than #553's larger allowances at the higher price.** The competitors read below show both models: Kajabi and ClickFunnels print large allowances in a higher price; HighLevel prints a base price and charges usage on top with no rate on its pricing page.
- Gumroad and Podia were not read (their pricing pages refused the fetch on 18 October 2026 in PR #553's reading); nothing is asserted about them.

## For the owner to decide

1. Whether to replace #553's prices with entry prices and packs at all: it cuts the printed included figures, which his rule of 18 October 2026 forbids without his decision.
2. If so, the price points (the rule above picks the lowest with at least 10% of #553's figures included; the tables show every other point and what it includes).
3. The pack sizes, and whether packs are offered at all for visits and orders (they are what a link-in-bio store sells through; when a window's figure is reached today, public pages rest and new orders stop).
